text:
incident-bot: URGENT: Paging oncall — `policy-engine` reported a runtime exception affecting smart-routing fallbacks. Severity: P1. @sara (oncall) @juan @mike

# Root message / paging
incident-bot: Source: policy-engine-v2 / runtime-exception / smart-routing. First observed at 2026-03-15T09:05:05Z. Error rate spike on routing decisions. Affected customers: multiple high-throughput tenants.

sara (oncall): I’m on it. Acknowledge and joining. Can someone post top-level symptoms?

juan: Seeing a spike in 5xx on route decision calls to /route/evaluate. Traffic shows rapid region fallbacks — requests keep bouncing from eu-west1 -> us-central1 -> eu-west1 in a loop for some customers.

mike: Logs show policy-engine process emitted a panic: `panic: invalid expression token` and then restarted by k8s liveness probe. Multiple restarts led to degraded routing state and fallbacks to older but incompatible model variants.

ashwin: Early impact numbers: ~18% of inference requests for customers X,Y,Z hit routing failures for last 20m. Latency for successful requests rose ~600ms due to extra routing hops before fallback.

ops-bot: Deployments: policy-engine-v2 rolled at 2026-03-15T08:45Z (commit ab3f2d). Autoscale triggered additional replicas 08:52Z. CrashLoopBackOff started 09:04Z.

# Initial triage
sara (oncall): Can we attach the panic stacktrace and the policy rule that triggered it?

juan: Pasting truncated stacktrace and offending rule below:

```
panic: runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0
goroutine 2783 [running]:
policy/engine.(*Evaluator).evalExpr(0xc000... , 0x7f, 0x0, 0x0)
	/go/src/redwood/policy/engine/evaluator.go:241 +0x2a7
policy/engine.EvaluateRouteDecision(0xc000...)
	/go/src/redwood/policy/engine/router.go:112 +0x1b3
... rest omitted
```

juan: And the rule that appears in the trace (from policy revision 2026-03-15T08:44):

```
- id: route_to_eu
  when: payload.region == "eu-*" && payload.model.variant[0].preferred == "high_throughput"
  route: eu-model-v3
```

juan: The expression `payload.model.variant[0].preferred` assumes variant is a non-empty array. In some model manifests variant is an empty list for the pinned fallback variants; evaluating index 0 causes the panic in our expression evaluator.

mike: That would explain the crash loop. The evaluator doesn't guard against empty arrays in this path — expression parser returns compiled AST that assumes indexing is safe. New validation in v2 should have caught it but the guard was omitted.

# Immediate mitigations
sara (oncall): Actions — 1) Hotfix: disable problematic policy revision 2) Roll traffic to safe default routing policy 3) Temp scale up dedicated routing instances to reduce latency/backpressure 4) Notify CS for customer impact. Who can disable the policy revision now?

ashwin: I’m rolling a policy rollback to revision 2026-03-15T08:30 (previous known-good). Executing: `redwoodctl policy rollback --service=smart-routing --rev=202603150830`

ops-bot: Command accepted. Policy rollback job started (job id 0a9c). Expected propagation to all evaluators in ~20s.

mike: Also toggled routing fallback to hard default: `config.smart_routing.force_default_model=true` in the configmap, applied across cluster. This will short-circuit evaluation and send to default-model for affected tenants.

ops-bot: Configmap updated in namespace redwood-prod. Restarting policy-engine pods to pick up config.

# Short-term effect and monitoring
eva: After rollback and config change, crash loops stopped. error-rate on /route/evaluate dropped from 18% -> 1.2% in 2 minutes. Latency is back down to baseline for most customers, some remain with transient increased latency due to queued requests.

cs-team-bot: Notifying CS: Created incident ticket INC-20260315-22 and sent standard customer impact template to account teams for X, Y, Z. Suggested message: "We observed intermittent routing failures affecting inference requests between 08:45 and 09:10 UTC; traffic has been restored to default routing and we are working on a fix."

# Post-remediation investigation notes
juan: Root cause: a new policy that introduced indexing into model.variant assumed non-empty lists. The policy author added a shorthand to prefer variants but didn't add a guard. The expression evaluator's runtime indexing operator doesn't validate bounds and triggers a panic on empty lists.

mike: Fix plan: two parts — runtime hardening (evaluator returns an expression-eval error instead of panicking when index out-of-range) and policy linter/CI to catch indexing into potentially-empty lists at upload time.

ashwin: I'll open a PR for the evaluator hardening (policy/evaluator: return evaluation error -> graceful false decision) and add tests for empty array indexing. Will tag @mike for review.

# Proposed immediate code change (sketch)
juan: Candidate fix (pseudocode):

```
func (e *Evaluator) evalIndex(node *IndexNode, ctx *evalCtx) (Value, error) {
  arr, err := e.eval(node.Subject, ctx)
  if err != nil { return Nil, err }
  if arr.Len() == 0 || node.Index >= arr.Len() {
    return Nil, fmt.Errorf("index out of range in expression")
  }
  return arr.Get(node.Index), nil
}
```

mike: We should also ensure `policy-upload` CI linter rejects policies containing `.variant[0]` without a guard like `len(payload.model.variant) > 0` or safe-index helper.

# Customer impact summary (for postmortem)
eva: Affected window: 2026-03-15T08:45Z -> 09:05Z (20m).
- Peak affected requests: ~18% of routed inference calls for ~3 enterprise tenants.
- Symptom: routing decisions failed with 5xx, causing fallbacks and routing loops.
- Business impact: several customers reported increased latency and failed inference calls; one realtime feature experienced outages for ~10 minutes.

cs-team-bot: CS outreach: initial messages dispatched to account leads. Follow-up scheduled at 13:00 UTC with detailed postmortem.

# Handoff and oncall notes
sara (oncall): I'm going to hand off to @mike for remediation work and PR. I'll remain available for escalation. Next oncall is @juan at 11:00 UTC.

mike: Acknowledged. Working on evaluator hardening PR now. Will link PR in this thread when ready.

# Followups / actions list
- [P1] Fix evaluator to return errors not panics on bad expressions (owner: mike; ETA: 2026-03-16 EOD).
- [P1] Add policy linter rule for safe indexing (owner: juan; ETA: 2026-03-17).
- [P2] Add policy upload runtime check to reject policies that reference `variant[0]` without a guard (owner: ashwin; ETA: 2026-03-18).
- [P3] Postmortem draft due 2026-03-18 12:00 UTC (owner: sara).

mike: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/policy/compare/bugfix/evaluator-index-guard (link will be updated with CI status).

incident-bot: Incident P1 created: INC-20260315-22. Duration: 00:20: - initial triage complete, mitigations applied.

sara (oncall): Great work team — nice and fast. We'll follow up with the postmortem and make sure CI & runtime both prevent this class of issue. :thumbsup:
